issues.t: Oil sludge and engine failure
issues.sym: The oil pressure light flickers at idle or stays on, then knocking or rattling, stalling, or the engine shutting off and not restarting. Many failures happen between about 70,000 and 145,000 miles.
issues.why: The 2.7L V6 is prone to oil breaking down into thick sludge that blocks oil flow, especially if oil changes are stretched out. Starved bearings and the timing chain then fail, sometimes breaking a connecting rod.
issues.next: Change the oil every 3,000–5,000 miles with the correct oil, and check the level often. If the oil light flickers or you hear knocking, stop driving and have the engine checked. A sludged engine usually needs replacing.

issues.t: Harsh, delayed or erratic shifting
issues.sym: Hard clunks when downshifting at low speed, a delay before the car moves, getting stuck in a low gear until restarted, or a check engine light with transmission codes.
issues.why: The automatic transmission in these Sebrings is known for shift problems from worn internal parts, solenoids and pressure sensors, or the transmission computer.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the fluid checked; use only the Chrysler-specified fluid. Sometimes a sensor, solenoid or computer update fixes it, but some cars need a rebuild.

issues.t: Automatic transmission failure
issues.sym: Slipping, flaring revs between shifts, harsh shifts, or the car stuck in one gear or not moving.
issues.why: The automatic transmission in this generation wears out, often around 90,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it slips or will not move, get a transmission diagnosis before more damage is done.

issues.t: Stalling or no-start from a failed distributor sensor
issues.sym: The engine stalls without warning, often once warm, or cranks but will not start. It may restart after cooling down.
issues.why: A sensor built into the distributor that tells the computer engine position fails, so the engine loses spark and fuel.
issues.next: Have a shop check for spark and position-sensor codes when it acts up. Replacing the distributor or its sensor usually fixes it.

issues.t: Failed emissions test
issues.sym: The check engine light is on, or the car fails a state smog or emissions test.
issues.why: Worn oxygen sensors, catalytic converters and related parts on high-mileage cars are the usual cause.
issues.next: Have the codes read before the test so you know which part is causing the failure.

issues.t: Front lower ball joints can separate (recalls)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end, wandering steering, or uneven tire wear. In the worst case the wheel can fold under the car.
issues.why: The rubber boots on the front lower ball joints can tear and let in water and dirt, so the joint wears or corrodes until it separates. Recalls 97V-201, 99V-066 and 00V-421 inspect and replace them.
issues.next: Have a dealer check all three ball joint recalls by VIN, and have the front end inspected if you hear clunks.

issues.t: Shifter can let the key come out when not in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The key may come out of the ignition with the shifter not in Park, or the shifter feels loose.
issues.why: A shifter cable adjustment problem can break a pin and defeat the park interlock. Recall 98V-183 replaces the shifter parts where needed.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Have a dealer check the recall.

issues.t: Throttle cable can fray and stick (recall)
issues.sym: The gas pedal feels sticky or does not return fully, so the engine stays revved.
issues.why: The throttle cable on cars with the 2.5L V6 can fray and bind. Recall 02V-186 replaces it.
issues.next: If the pedal sticks, shift to Neutral, brake and pull over. Have the recall checked.

issues.t: Brake booster vacuum hose installed wrong (recall)
issues.sym: A hard brake pedal or longer stops.
issues.why: On convertibles with the 2.5L V6, the vacuum hose for the power brake booster was installed incorrectly. Recall 96V-123 fixes it.
issues.next: If the brake pedal feels hard, do not drive until it is checked. Have the recall done.

issues.t: Crank sensor wiring can short and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine suddenly stalls while driving and may not restart right away.
issues.why: The crankshaft sensor wiring could touch a new heat shield and short to ground. Recall 00V-299 reroutes it.
issues.next: Have the recall checked. If it stalls in traffic, get safely off the road.

issues.t: Transmission cooler hoses can leak (recall)
issues.sym: Red fluid under the front of the car, smoke from the engine bay, or poor shifting.
issues.why: The transmission cooler hoses can leak fluid onto hot parts. Recall 01V-011 replaces them.
issues.next: Check for red fluid drips and have the recall done.

issues.t: Sun visor can come loose when the airbag fires (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign before a crash.
issues.why: The passenger sun visor can break free when the passenger airbag deploys and hit the occupant. Recalls 15V-338 and 16V-401 add a tether.
issues.next: Have a dealer check both recalls by VIN.

issues.t: Fuel return line can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell, fuel drips, or fuel wetness near the tank or lines.
issues.why: A restricted fitting in the fuel return line can raise fuel pressure and make a hose leak (recall 03V-443). Some 2004 two-door cars also have a poorly molded return hose fitting that can break (recall 04V-313).
issues.next: Do not drive with a fuel smell. Have a dealer check both recalls by VIN.

issues.t: Right steering knuckle may crack (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the right front, wandering steering, or the wheel looking out of line.
issues.why: Some right steering knuckles were damaged during manufacturing and can crack and separate. Recall 04V-579 replaces it.
issues.next: Have the recall checked by VIN. Any new front-end clunk should be inspected right away.

issues.t: Rear spring seat cracks and clunks
issues.sym: Clunking or squeaking from the rear over bumps, and in bad cases a loose rear strut.
issues.why: The aluminum spring seat castings in the rear suspension can crack or corrode.
issues.next: Have the rear struts and spring seats inspected. Replace cracked parts on both sides before the strut comes loose.

issues.t: Blower fan works only on high
issues.sym: The heater and A/C fan only blows on the highest setting, or some speeds stop working.
issues.why: The blower motor resistor, which sets the lower fan speeds, burns out.
issues.next: Replace the blower motor resistor; it is a small, inexpensive part. If it keeps failing, have the blower motor checked too.

issues.t: Heater blows cold
issues.sym: Little or no heat from the vents, sometimes with the check engine light on.
issues.why: A stuck-open thermostat keeps the engine from warming up and sets a code; low coolant or a clogged heater core also cuts heat.
issues.next: Check the coolant level first, then have the thermostat and heater core checked.

issues.t: Stalls when coming to a stop
issues.sym: The engine dies as you slow down or stop at a light.
issues.why: Dirty throttle bodies, idle control problems or sensor faults are typical causes on these cars.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the throttle body cleaned. Get it fixed soon, since stalling in traffic is dangerous.

issues.t: Horn goes off by itself
issues.sym: The horn sounds on its own, sometimes for a long time while the car is parked and locked, often late at night.
issues.why: The horn switch in the steering wheel pad or the clock spring behind it fails and shorts.
issues.next: Pull the horn fuse or relay as a stopgap. The usual fix is replacing the steering wheel horn switch; a technician should handle it because it sits with the airbag.

issues.t: Engine stalls at stops or while driving
issues.sym: The engine shuts off at a light, while braking, or while driving, while the lights and radio stay on. It often restarts.
issues.why: No single cause has been confirmed. A recall (08V-152) covers a corroding tire pressure sensor connector that can cause stalling, but many owners report stalls where dealers find no code or cause.
issues.next: Make sure all recalls are done. Write down when it happens (damp weather, braking, idle) to help a shop find it, and have the engine computer checked for updates.

issues.t: Tire pressure sensor connector can short (recall)
issues.sym: No-start, a dead battery, or stalling.
issues.why: An unused tire pressure monitor connector can corrode and short out. Recall 08V-152 covers it.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the VIN, especially if the car stalls or drains the battery.

issues.t: Radiator fan connector can short and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from the front of the engine bay.
issues.why: On cars with the 2.4L engine, coolant can be drawn into the left radiator fan motor connector and short it. Recall 07V-473 covers it.
issues.next: Have the recall checked right away.

issues.t: Seat position sensors for airbags may fail (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag light may come on.
issues.why: Front seat track position sensors, which tell the airbags how close you sit, may not work right. Recall 07V-240 covers it.
issues.next: Have the recall checked; an airbag light means the system may not work right.

issues.t: ABS software can lock the rear brakes (recall)
issues.sym: The rear wheels lock up during hard braking, making the car slide.
issues.why: The anti-lock brake computer software could lock the rear brakes in certain stops. Recall 06V-493 updates it.
issues.next: Have the recall done by VIN.

issues.t: Hood can open while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The hood pops or flutters at speed.
issues.why: The hood latch striker can break. Recall 06V-431 covers it.
issues.next: Have the recall done; if the hood flutters, slow down and pull over.

issues.t: Windshield defroster can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The defroster does not clear fog or frost from the windshield.
issues.why: On cars with automatic climate control, the HVAC software could turn off the defrost function. Recall 06V-494 updates it.
issues.next: Have the recall done before winter.

issues.t: Paint peeling and bubbling
issues.sym: Paint bubbles, peels or flakes off, often on the roof, hood and trunk.
issues.why: The factory paint or clear coat lets go from the surface.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about paint coverage, then get repaint quotes. Keep bare spots sealed to slow rust.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads higher than actual (recall)
issues.sym: The car runs out of gas while the gauge still shows fuel.
issues.why: On 2.4L cars, a software problem can make the gauge show more fuel than is in the tank. Recall 09V-047 updates it.
issues.next: Use the trip odometer to track fuel until the recall is done.

issues.t: Engine computer circuit board can crack and stall (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls suddenly and may not restart.
issues.why: A new adhesive in the engine computer can crack its circuit board. Recall 08V-528 covers it.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the VIN.

issues.t: Airbags and seat belt pretensioners may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag light may come on.
issues.why: A short in the occupant restraint control module can stop the airbags and pretensioners from working in a crash. Recall 16V-668 covers it.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the VIN.

issues.t: Power steering hose can leak and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leaking, a burning smell, or whining steering.
issues.why: The power steering pressure hose can separate at its crimp and spray fluid on hot parts. Recall 10V-475 covers it.
issues.next: If you smell burning fluid, stop and have it checked. Have the recall done.

issues.t: Brake booster clip may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before the brakes suddenly do not respond.
issues.why: The clip that holds the brake pedal to the brake booster rod may be missing or formed wrong. Recall 10V-009 covers it.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the VIN right away.

issues.t: Battery won't hold a charge
issues.sym: The car won't start after sitting, or the battery dies repeatedly even after being replaced.
issues.why: Owners report weak batteries and drains, sometimes linked to charging system or electrical faults.
issues.next: Have the battery, alternator and any parasitic drain tested before buying another battery.

issues.t: Brakes wear out early
issues.sym: Grinding or squealing brakes, or pads and rotors needing replacement well before 40,000 miles.
issues.why: Owners report brake pads and rotors wearing out early.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected at each oil change and replace pads before they reach the rotors.

issues.t: Rusted front subframe
issues.sym: Clunks from the front end, poor alignment, or a failed safety inspection for rust.
issues.why: The front subframe can rust badly on high-mileage cars in salt-belt states.
issues.next: Have the subframe inspected for rust at each service. A badly rotted subframe must be replaced before it fails.
